sections: The Trade You Could Only Half Explain
Question One: What Is The Idea?

cues.text: You saw it go. A long red bar at 9:47 a.m., through nothing in particular. You sold the break of the next bar; the move was real. Stop above that high.
Two minutes later price came back through your entry. You could name the bar. Not the level, not the price where you were wrong. No idea.
A third of a trade: an entry event with nothing above it. The bar could not name one thing above itself.
Every trade traces up one chain: the idea; the setup, a location and a read; the trigger, the price event there; then construction, the arithmetic.
Three questions in a fixed order. The order is the rule: each answer only means something inside the one above it.
Question one: what is the idea? A conditional written before the session: an if-then thesis at a named level, a price marked before the open.
The invalidation, the price that ends it. A conviction: strong, moderate or thin.

If price accepts below the on-low zone, the overnight low, a 5-minute close under it, and a Pause N Go, Module 13's trigger, fires on the pullback, then pd-val, the prior day's value low. Wrong on a 5-minute close above it. Conviction moderate.
Nothing in it says where the market goes. Catalyst, calendar, range and value enter here, Module 9's inputs: an idea, never an entry.
Five things feel like ideas and are not one.
One: a day-type label. Trend day is a forecast about the whole session. Nothing proves it wrong at 9:45.
Two: the overnight's direction. It builds levels for your list, never a direction.
Three: an indicator or another market. Neither ever sets the thesis.
Four: a catalyst alone. It moves conviction, creates no level and waives none.
Five: dealer positioning. A gamma regime, Module 4, is a note beside the conviction label: never a location, never a change to the count.
The rule: the idea is written before the session, at a named level, with its invalidation price, timeframe and conviction. No named invalidation: No Setup, the tag for a trade taken on feel.
Getting it wrong is shorting because it has to stop, nothing written. It reveals a bet on a direction with no price where you are wrong. The stop is the only argument.
The fix: no order without an idea line on the pre-market sheet, written by 9:25, a number and a timeframe in its invalidation. No line: No Setup, whatever it made.

options: The invalidation: the price that ends it
check.why: Thesis, invalidation and conviction. Nothing in an idea says where the market will go.

check.q: “Trend day” is written on the sheet as the idea. What is wrong with it?
options: No price can prove it wrong at 9:45; it is a forecast, not an idea
It should name the overnight direction too
check.why: A day-type label describes the whole session. An idea names a level and the price at which it is wrong.

check.q: A line on the sheet names a level and a target but no invalidation. What is a trade taken from it?
options: An A trade with a note
No Setup, however good it sounds
check.why: An idea without a named invalidation is No Setup. The tag is written the same session, whatever the trade made.

check.q: A move has run a long way and you short it “because it has to stop”, nothing written. What does it reveal?
options: A bet on a direction with no price at which you are wrong
check.why: With no invalidation the stop becomes the only argument you respect. The fix is an idea line on the sheet by 9:25.

cues.text: Question two: where, and what is price doing there? The setup is a named location plus the read of what price is doing there, judged on a closed bar.
The location is one level from your list, written as a zone: a band with a near edge and a far edge, the stop behind the far edge. Logged by its slug, its short name, like on-low.
Two halves, and the order matters: where first, then what. The where is a zone from the Module 6 list: on-low, pd-high, pd-val, an opening-range extreme once its window has closed.
The what is a read you can see on a closed bar. Acceptance, a 5-minute close beyond the zone within 15 minutes of the first touch, is the read for Trend Continuation, Module 10.
A failure back through a range extreme is Range Rejection, Module 11, a context read with no entry of its own. A gap, an open outside the prior day's range, has its own setups, Module 12.

The same footprint event, Module 7's print of buying or selling, means different things in different places. Aggressive selling at a session high is a read. Halfway between two levels, it is a print with nothing to stand on.
VWAP, moving averages, pivots, Fibonacci levels and round numbers are not locations. Neither is the inside of the initial balance, the first hour's range, or the middle of a balance range.
A round number is easy to see. So is the middle of the room. Nothing stands behind either.
Any price outside every zone on your list is mid-range: no named level, nothing for a stop to sit behind. The tag exists so a trade there is counted, not hidden.
The rule: the setup names one slug, written as a zone, and one read seen on a closed bar. If you cannot name the slug, the location is mid-range, and the trade is tagged that way.
Getting it wrong is Trigger Without Location: a bar pattern or a burst of movement acted on in the middle of nowhere, usually early, when everything moves.
It reveals reacting to movement, not to a place. A stop with no structure behind it is a guess about how far noise will go.
The fix: every zone on your list carries two platform alerts, one at each edge, Module 17. No alert, no setup, and your hand stays off the order buttons.
When you write the sentence before entry, the slug is the first word.

segments.title: Question three, and construction
sections: Question Three: What Just Happened At The Level?
Then Construction: Level, Stop, Risk, Size, Entry

cues.text: Question three: what just happened at the level? The trigger is the price event there that says enter now. Order flow can confirm it, never fire it.
Pause N Go. After the first touch, at least two consecutive 1-minute bars hold inside the zone, no 1-minute close through the far edge. The pause.
Then a 1-minute close beyond the pause's extreme, with the read. The go. Entry on that close.
A resting limit is a trigger only after price has displaced, moved away from the level first. Placed blind, its field is blank. Indicators never trigger.
The rule: something must happen at the level before entry, a named price event. No trigger, no position. Nothing fired: the field is blank, and a blank is data.
Getting it wrong is selling the first touch because the idea and level were right. It reveals trusting your idea over the market's answer. The level asks. The trigger replies.
The fix: the branch, one if-then line of your plan, names its trigger before the session. The order goes on the closed bar that completes it, or a limit named in advance.
Then construction: the arithmetic that turns three answers into an order, after the tiers, never before. A short below a zone:
One: level. The zone traded against, and the target, the level the trade aims at. Both on the sheet.
Two: stop. A resting order behind the far edge, placed with the entry. A wider stop floor, the smallest stop allowed at that hour, Module 14, pushes it out to the floor.
Three: risk. Entry to stop, in points and ticks. A target under twice that is no trade. 2 to 1 is a filter, not a target.
Four: size. One base R, the fixed amount you risk on one trade, divided by the stop's value per contract, rounded down.
Five: entry. The order, its intended price written down so the fill can be measured. Full or half size by grade is Module 14's table.
The rule: construction runs in this order, after the three answers. The stop is found on the chart. The size is computed from it.
Getting it wrong is the contract count chosen first, the stop wherever the loss feels bearable. It reveals the money deciding the structure: a stop inside the noise.
The fix: write the stop price before the size, every time. An impossible stop means the entry drifted from the level. The stop did not move. The entry did.

segments.title: One sentence, the grade, and the tier you skip
sections: The Grade Checks The Tiers At Entry
The Tier You Skip When You Want To Be In

cues.text: The tiers fit one sentence, and the sentence is the test. If the read, at the zone, and the trigger fires, then the target. Wrong on the invalidation. Conviction.
The read and the zone are the setup. The trigger is the trigger. Target, invalidation and conviction are the idea. Two of three is not a lighter trade; it carries the missing tier's tag.
The rule: before every entry the sentence is complete, aloud, in this order, every slot on the chart. Where you stall names the missing tier: no order, and a tally mark.
Getting it wrong is a sentence that trails off: short here because, it's heavy. Heavy is not a slot. It reveals the skipped tier, caught before the trade.
The grade is the entry-plan score, given at entry, before the trade resolves: A-plus, A, B or C, from four checks. The checks are the tiers.
One: the location is a named level. Fails when it is mid-range.
Two: the trigger fired before entry. Fails on a blank field, or an early order.
Three: the stop is behind structure. Fails inside the noise, short of the edge.
Four: the size matches the plan for that stop. Fails when size came first.
A-plus: all four, and a fill within 2 ticks of intended.
A: all four.
B: three of four, no breach of stop or size.
C: two or fewer, or any breach. No trade.
The grade reads the plan, never the outcome. A losing A-plus is a normal member of the distribution. A winning C is a warning, the trade that teaches the wrong lesson.
The rule: the grade is written at entry, from the four checks, and never changes.
Getting it wrong is winners graded A, losers C: grading the market, not your process. The fix: four yes-or-no boxes within a minute of entry, trade open.
The hard part. The trigger is the only tier with a feeling attached. An idea is a line; a level, a price on a list. A trigger moves, and movement makes you want in.
So the trade is built downward from the bar, worst after a run of winners or a missed move. Missing a trade costs nothing. Forcing one costs the tiers, then the R.
The rule: trace a trade up from the idea, never down from the bar. Every entry explained by its bar, none by its level, reveals the wish to be in. The fix: the same tally mark.

options: The target, the invalidation and the conviction
check.why: The read and the zone are the setup, the trigger is the trigger, and the rest is the idea. Two of three carries the tag of the missing tier.

check.q: All four checks pass and the fill is 3 ticks from the intended price. What is the grade?
check.why: A is all four. A+ needs the four plus a fill within 2 ticks of the intended price.

check.q: Three of four pass; the one that failed is the stop, which sat inside the noise. What is the grade?
options: C: a breach of the stop or size check
check.why: B needs three of four with no breach of the stop or size check. Any breach of those two is C, and C is no trade.

check.q: Every entry in a session can be explained by the bar that triggered it, none by the level. What does it reveal?
options: The wish to be in the market replacing the plan for being in a trade
check.why: The trigger became a reason instead of a reply. The fix is a count: one tally mark each time the hand moves before the sentence ends.

cues.text: A hypothetical illustration, not a trade record: a composite MNQ morning, invented prices. It stops with the order working, before any outcome.
Question one, the idea, written at 9:10 on the sheet. If price accepts below the on-low zone, 20,262 to 20,272, and a Pause N Go fires on the pullback into it, then pd-val at 20,176.
Wrong on a 5-minute close back above 20,272. Conviction moderate: one level in the zone. Price returns from underneath, so the far edge for this trade is the top, 20,272.

Question two, the setup. The first touch prints at 10:02. The 10:05 to 10:10 5-minute bar closes at 20,256.25, below 20,262, eight minutes after the touch. Accepted below. Setup: trend-continuation. Location: on-low.

Question three, the trigger. Price pulls back into the zone. The 10:13 and 10:14 1-minute bars hold inside, no close above 20,272: the pause, low 20,263.50. The 10:15 bar closes at 20,261.75, below it. The go.
Delta, buying minus selling, was failing on the pullback, so the confirmation field gets failing-delta. It confirmed. It did not fire. Trigger field: pause-n-go.
Construction at 10:15. Level: the zone and the target, chosen at 9:10. Stop: 20,274, behind the far edge, above the pause high.
Risk: 12.25 points, 49 ticks. The target is seven times that, so 2 to 1 clears.
Size: one base R divided by the value of 49 ticks per contract, rounded down. Entry: sell the 10:15 close, intended 20,261.75, stop sent with it. Fill, one tick away.
Grade at entry: named level, trigger fired, stop behind structure, size from the plan, fill within 2 ticks. All yes. A-plus, written at 10:16 with the trade open.
Traced up: the order exists because a trigger fired, inside a named zone, after acceptance, where a line at 9:10 named it. Take away any one and the order has no reason left. The case stops here.
The same morning, at 9:47 a.m.: price falls forty points in four minutes and the archetype with a trigger and no level sells the close, stop above the bar, usual size.
Trace it up. Blank trigger. Mid-range. No Setup. Grade C: no trade.
Both were short, on the same morning. The chart drew the same structure for both. It did not know which one had a sheet.

cues.text: Your score. Take your last ten trades. For each, one point per line that is true, tracing up from the entry.
One: trigger. A named trigger from Module 13 completed before the order went in. A blank scores zero.
Two: setup. The location a slug from your list, written as a zone, the read on a closed bar. Mid-range scores zero.
Three: idea. A line written before the session named this level, with an invalidation price, a timeframe and a conviction.
Four: construction. Stop behind the far edge, placed with the entry; target clearing 2 to 1; size from the stop distance.
Four of four is a complete trade. Count down each line, not across each trade. Any line missed on two or more of the ten is your skip.
More than one line over: fix the highest tier first, idea, setup, trigger, construction, because each tier only means something inside the one above it.
Line three is fixed on the sheet before the open; two with the zone alerts; one with the closed-bar rule; four by writing the stop before the size.
Getting it wrong is scoring from memory. Memory keeps a tidy journal; every trade in it had a level. It reveals a record kept in your head. Score from the journal.
Before your next session, one thing. Before each entry, say one sentence aloud in tier order: the idea with its invalidation, the zone and the read, the trigger that just fired.
If the sentence does not finish, the order does not go in. That is the whole assignment.
In one line: a trade is three answers in a fixed order, then the arithmetic. Missing one, it is not a smaller trade. It is a different thing, with a tag that says so.
Where it goes next. Module 9, Idea Generation, is the first tier: how the inputs become a thesis, an invalidation and a conviction.
The second tier draws on Module 6 for the level list and Modules 10 to 12 for the reads. Module 13 teaches each trigger, Module 7's order flow confirming.
Module 14, Trade Construction, carries the arithmetic and the one table that turns a grade into a size. Module 15 makes the sentence a written branch; Module 16, an idea line.
In the journal, Module 18, each tier has its field: setup, location, trigger and grade. No Setup, mid-range and a blank trigger are how a skipped tier shows up in your record, not your memory.

check.q: How is the score read?
options: Across each trade, best trade first
Count down each line: any line missed on two or more of ten is your skip
check.why: A line missed on two or more of ten trades is the tier you skip. More than one, fix the highest tier first.

check.q: Lines two and three both miss on three of ten. Which do you fix first?
options: Line three, the idea: the highest tier
check.why: Idea, then setup, then trigger, then construction, because each tier only means something inside the one above it.

check.q: You score the ten trades from memory. What does it reveal?
options: A record kept in your head; the journal is where No Setup is written
check.why: Memory keeps a tidy journal. Score from the journal, where a missed line three reads No Setup, whatever the trade made.

check.q: What is the assignment for your next session?
options: Say one sentence aloud in tier order before each entry; if it does not finish, no order
Grade every trade after the close
check.why: The idea with its invalidation, then the zone and the read, then the trigger that just fired. That is the whole assignment.

questions.q: What is the order of the chain every trade traces up through?
questions.why: Idea first, then setup, then trigger, then the arithmetic. Each answer only means something inside the one above it.

questions.q: Which of these is an idea?
options: “If price accepts below on-low and a Pause N Go fires on the pullback, then pd-val. Wrong on a 5-minute close above the top edge. Conviction moderate.”
questions.why: A conditional at a named level, with the price that ends it and a conviction grade. The other three name no price at which they are wrong.

questions.q: What is the location of a trade taken outside every zone on your list?
options: Mid-range, and it is counted rather than hidden
questions.why: No named level, nothing for a stop to sit behind. The tag exists so the trade is counted.

questions.q: Where does order flow sit in the tiers?
options: It confirms a trigger and is recorded; it is never the trigger
questions.why: A recorded sub-form plus a price event. The price event is the trigger.
The stop is found on the chart and the size is computed from it. A wider stop means fewer contracts, never more risk.

questions.q: Which tier does grade check 3, stop behind structure, read?
questions.why: Checks 1 and 2 read the setup and the trigger. Checks 3 and 4, stop and size, read construction. The idea is checked earlier, on the sheet.

questions.q: Why is the trigger the tier most often skipped?
options: It is the hardest to define
It comes last in the journal
It is the only tier with a feeling attached: movement makes you want to be in
questions.why: An idea is a written line and a level is a price on a list. The fix is a tally mark each time the hand goes first.

questions.q: In the worked case, why did the 10:15 order exist?
options: Because a trigger fired inside a named zone, after acceptance, where a line at 9:10 named it
questions.why: Take away any one of the three and the order has no reason left. The case stops with the order working.
